Download the companion pSI data sets (the former pSI.data package)

Source: R/psi_data.R
psi_data.Rd

psi_data fetches the precomputed Specificity Index (pSI) tables that used to be distributed as the companion package pSI.data: mouse cell types profiled by bacTRAP, and human brain regions from BrainSpan. They are too large for CRAN (about 10 MB together), so they are published as a release on the pSI GitHub repository and downloaded on first use.

Usage

psi_data(dataset = c("mouse", "human"), cache = NULL, quiet = FALSE)

Source

https://github.com/DunderChief/pSI/releases/tag/pSI.data-1.0. Mouse expression data from GEO series GSE13379 and GSE30626; human data from the BrainSpan Atlas of the Developing Human Brain, https://www.brainspan.org.

Arguments

dataset

"mouse" or "human".

cache

logical or NULL; see Details.

quiet

logical. If TRUE, no download messages are shown.

Value

The requested data set, a named list of data frames as described above. If the file is not already available and cannot be downloaded (for example when offline), NULL is returned invisibly with a message rather than an error.

Details

The two data sets, unchanged from pSI.data 1.0 (2014):

"mouse"

a list of three data frames of 16907 genes by 35 mouse cell types or regions, profiled by translating ribosome affinity purification (bacTRAP) on one microarray platform, as of October 2013: psi.in (averaged expression values), psi.in.filter (NA marks genes to exclude for a cell type) and psi.out (pSI values).

"human"

a list of two aggregations of BrainSpan RNA-seq data for 16866 genes: developmental.periods (six brain regions across ten developmental periods, 60 columns) and young.adulthood (the same six regions for young adulthood only). Each holds psi.in and psi.out.

The psi.out tables are ready to use as the pSIs argument of fisher.iteration, candidate.overlap, pSI.list and pSI.count.

Every download is verified against the file's MD5 checksum. Where the file is kept depends on cache. With cache = TRUE it goes under the package's user cache directory, tools::R_user_dir("pSI", "cache"), so later R sessions reuse it. With cache = FALSE it goes under tempdir() and disappears with the session. The default, NULL, asks you once per session when R is interactive and otherwise behaves like FALSE. To skip the question in every session, set options(pSI.data.cache = TRUE) (or FALSE) in your .Rprofile. To delete the cached files, remove that directory: unlink(tools::R_user_dir("pSI", "cache"), recursive = TRUE).

See also

sample.data for the small built-in example data.

Examples

# \donttest{
## about 4 MB, kept only for this session
mouse <- psi_data("mouse", cache = FALSE)
#> Downloading mouse.rda (4.3 MB) from https://github.com/DunderChief/pSI/releases/download/pSI.data-1.0/mouse.rda
if (!is.null(mouse)) {
  names(mouse)
  dim(mouse$psi.out)
  ## CSEA: is the AutDB candidate list enriched in any mouse cell type?
  fisher.iteration(mouse$psi.out, candidate.genes$AutDB)
}
